title: OCTA: 9.8M Filipino families consider themselves poor in Q3 2026
summary: An estimated 9.8 million Filipino families, or 37% of respondents, considered themselves poor in the third quarter of 2026, the latest survey of OCTA Research showed.

blocks.text: Published November 25, 2026 9:50am
An estimated 9.8 million Filipino families, or 37% of respondents, considered themselves poor in the third quarter of 2026, the latest survey of OCTA Research showed.
This is considered statistically unchanged from the 39% or about 10.3 million families in the second quarter of the year as it is within the survey's ±3% margin of error, OCTA said.
Meanwhile, 42% can't say if they are poor or not poor, and 21% said they are not poor.
The Tugon ng Masa non-commissioned survey also showed that 56% of respondents in Mindanao rated themselves poor.
This was followed by 49% in Visayas, 26% in Balance Luzon or the rest of Luzon except for Metro Manila, and 20% in the National Capital Region.
By income class, 52% of those in Class E rated themselves as poor. Among those in Class D, 38% considered themselves poor, while 17% of Class ABC saw themselves as poor.

"Among families reporting poverty, the median monthly household-expense threshold was P18,000, and the median additional amount lacking was P5,000. These are self-reported amounts, not official poverty lines," OCTA Research said.
Self-rated hunger
Meanwhile, 22% or about 5.8 million families said they experienced involuntary hunger or had nothing to eat at least once in the three months preceding the survey in the third quarter of the year.
OCTA said this shows self-rated hunger is statistically unchanged from the 21% (5.6 million families) recorded in the second quarter.
Seventy-eight percent on the other hand said they did not experience hunger even once during the last three months.
Source: OCTA Research
"Among families that experienced hunger, about 83% said it happened only once or a few times," OCTA said.
At 29%, the National Capital Region and Visayas showed the highest incidence of hunger among geographic areas.
Nearly half or 49% of respondents in Class E meanwhile said they experienced hunger.
Self-rated food poverty
Also statistically unchanged is the self-rated food poverty for the third quarter at 27% or about 7.1 million families.
In the second quarter, 28% or 7.4 million families regarded themselves as food-poor.
"Meanwhile, the share who considered their families not food-poor increased from 27% to 33%, and the undecided share declined from 45% to 40%," OCTA said.
"Food poverty refers to situations in which individuals and households struggle to obtain sufficient and healthful food," it added.
The survey showed that in Mindanao, 54% of respondents considered themselves as food-poor.
It was followed by Visayas at 35%, Balance Luzon at 16%, and NCR at 10%.
"By socioeconomic class, 34% of Class E families considered themselves food-poor, compared with 30% in Class D and 6% in Class ABC," OCTA said.
Survey details
The survey was conducted from September 28 to October 4 via face-to-face interviews among 1,200 male and female adults.
Margin of error is at ±3% at a 95% confidence level.

"Subnational estimates for the geographic areas covered in the survey have the following margins of error at a 95% confidence level: ±6% for NCR, Balance Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao," OCTA said. —KG, GMA News
